faqPage.title: Frequently asked questions
faqPage.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Presence and website monitoring.
faqPage.ctaText: Check your website for free — no account required.

i1.a: Website monitoring is the automated, continuous process of checking whether your website is accessible, performing well, and correctly configured. A monitoring service like Presence checks your website regularly — every hour or more — and alerts you immediately if something goes wrong.

i2.q: Why should I monitor my website?
i2.a: Your website is often the first thing a potential customer sees. If it's offline, loading slowly, or showing a security warning, visitors leave immediately. Website monitoring ensures you're always the first to know about problems — before your customers notice.

i3.q: Does Presence work for small businesses?
i3.a: Absolutely. Presence is designed specifically for small business owners who don't have a technical team. Everything is explained in plain language, and you don't need any technical knowledge to use it.

i4.q: Does Presence change or access my website?
i4.a: No. Presence only checks publicly available information about your website — the same information a visitor or search engine would see. We never access your files, database, or CMS.

i1.q: How often is my website checked?
i1.a: On the Pro plan, your website is checked every hour automatically. On the Business plan, checks happen even more frequently. On the Free plan, you can run checks manually at any time.

i2.a: Presence monitors website availability, SSL certificate validity, DNS configuration, email security (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), security headers, website performance, uptime statistics, and online reviews.

i3.a: Presence sends a request to your website on a regular schedule and records whether your website responded successfully. The results are compiled into your uptime history, giving you an accurate record of your website availability over time.

i4.q: What happens if my website goes offline?
i4.a: You receive an immediate alert by email or push notification. Presence continues monitoring and sends another notification as soon as your website comes back online.

i5.a: Yes. Depending on your plan, you can monitor 1, 10, 50 or 200 websites from the same dashboard.

i1.a: Presence checks your SSL certificate every day. It verifies that your certificate is valid, trusted by major browsers, and tracks its expiry date. You receive an alert 30 days before your certificate expires.

i2.a: DNS monitoring tracks your domain's DNS records and alerts you when they change unexpectedly. Unexpected DNS changes can indicate account compromises, configuration errors, or unauthorized modifications.

i3.q: What are SPF, DKIM and DMARC?
i3.a: SPF, DKIM and DMARC are email authentication standards that protect your domain from email spoofing. SPF specifies which servers can send email on your behalf. DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to your emails. DMARC tells email providers what to do with unauthenticated emails.

i4.q: Why is email security important for small businesses?
i4.a: Without proper email security, anyone can send emails that appear to come from your domain — phishing your customers and damaging your reputation. SPF, DKIM and DMARC significantly reduce this risk.

i5.a: Security headers are HTTP response headers that instruct browsers to behave safely. Common examples include X-Frame-Options (prevents your site from being embedded in iframes), Content-Security-Policy (restricts which resources can load), and HSTS (forces HTTPS).

i1.q: Can I install Presence as a mobile app?
i1.a: Yes. Presence is a Progressive Web App (PWA). You can install it on your iPhone, Android phone, or computer directly from your browser — no app store required. It works like a native app with push notifications.

i2.q: How do I install Presence on my phone?
i2.a: On Android: open Presence in Chrome and tap 'Add to home screen' in the browser menu. On iOS: open Presence in Safari, tap the Share button, and select 'Add to Home Screen'.

i3.a: Yes. Presence caches your most recent dashboard data so you can view it even when you're offline. The data will be updated as soon as your connection is restored.

i1.a: Yes. There are no long-term contracts. You can cancel your subscription at any time from your account settings. Your account remains active until the end of the current billing period.

i2.a: All paid plans include a 14-day free trial. No credit card is required to start your trial.

i3.q: What's included in the free plan?
i3.a: The free plan includes 1 website, 10 scans per month and email notifications. It's a great way to start and see what Presence can do before upgrading.

i4.a: Yes. Presence collects only the information necessary to monitor your digital presence. We use encrypted connections, secure data storage, and are GDPR compliant.

legal.privacySubtitle: How Presence processes personal data, which rights you have and which service providers are involved — working draft, to be reviewed before launch.
legal.privacyIntro: This privacy policy describes which personal data Presence processes to run the monitoring service. It is a working draft: the text reflects what the product technically does but has not been reviewed by a qualified person yet. Content in square brackets must be completed before launch.
legal.privacyControllerBody: The controller for the processing of personal data within the meaning of the GDPR is the provider named in the imprint. Company name, address and a reachable e-mail address are marked as placeholders there and must be completed before launch. Whether a data protection officer has to be appointed must be assessed before launch.
privacyDataItems: Account data: name, e-mail address, password (stored only as a hash) and the plan you choose when registering.
Website data: domains and URLs you add for monitoring, together with their scan and notification settings.

Scan data: publicly retrievable technical information about your domains, such as certificate details, DNS records, e-mail security records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), HTTP security headers, reachability and response times. This information can generally be retrieved by any visitor to your website as well.

Usage data: technical access data on our API (requested path, HTTP method, status code, timestamp, shortened user agent, referrer) and a hashed, never plain-text IP address for reach measurement and abuse detection.
Payment and subscription data: payment processing runs through Paddle as merchant of record. Card details are never transmitted to us; we receive the subscription status we need to unlock the plans.
Communication data: messages you send us through the contact form or support channels.
privacyPurposeItems: Providing the service: account, sign-in and display of the monitored websites and scan results.
Running the scans you start and producing the associated reports.
Notifications: sending alerts when you have enabled them in your settings.
Subscription and billing: managing the plan, enforcing the applicable usage limits and invoicing through Paddle.
Operational security: detecting abuse and attacks, analysing errors and technically logging API requests.
Legal obligations: meeting commercial and tax retention duties.
legal.privacyLawfulIntro: Depending on the operation, we rely on the following legal bases. The mapping must be confirmed legally before launch.
privacyLawfulItems: Performance of a contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR): account, scans, reports, notifications and subscription management.
Legitimate interests (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR): operational security, abuse detection and server-side reach measurement based on hashed IP addresses.
Legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR): retention of invoices and accounting records.
Consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR): only where we expressly obtain it for individual purposes; you can withdraw consent at any time with effect for the future.
legal.privacyAiTitle: AKA IA: explanations produced by an AI feature
legal.privacyAiBody: Presence includes an optional AI feature (AKA IA) that explains scan results and drafts suggested actions. When you use it, we transmit your input and the technical details of the selected scan — such as the domain, the status of individual checks and the severity of findings — to the configured AI interface. The answers are machine-generated, may be incomplete or factually wrong and do not replace a professional security assessment; they are no guarantee that a website is secure. Which provider operates the interface and whether data is processed outside the EU must be documented and settled contractually before launch.
legal.privacySharingIntro: We do not sell personal data. Service providers receive only the data their task requires. For every provider, a data processing agreement and — where processing happens outside the EU — a transfer basis must be reviewed before launch.
privacySharingItems: Payment provider (Paddle): subscription management, payment and invoicing; Paddle acts as merchant of record.
Hosting and infrastructure for the application, database, cache and scans. [Enter provider and server location before launch.]
E-mail delivery for transactional messages such as confirmation links, password resets and alerts. [Enter provider before launch.]
AI interface for AKA IA when you use the feature. [Enter provider and place of processing before launch.]

Editorial system for the blog (WordPress): the blog runs in its own, separate system. The application only retrieves published posts through the public interface; editorial credentials are never delivered to the public site.
legal.privacyRetentionBody: We store account data and the websites you register for as long as your account exists. Scan results and reports remain retrievable with the account. When you delete your account, we remove the account and the data attached to it immediately — there is no 30-day waiting period. The only exception is data we must keep under commercial or tax retention duties, such as invoices. Which periods apply and how they are enforced at the payment provider must be defined before launch.
legal.privacyRightsIntro: Under the GDPR you have in particular the following rights:
privacyRightsItems: Access to the data processed about you (Art. 15 GDPR)
Objection to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21 GDPR)
Withdrawal of consent you have given (Art. 7(3) GDPR)
legal.privacyRightsHow: You can assemble access and data export yourself in your account settings; for anything else a message through the contact form is enough. You may also lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority — competent is the authority at your habitual residence or the authority at the controller's seat.
legal.privacySecurityBody: We protect your data with encrypted transmission (HTTPS/TLS), exclusively hashed passwords and server-side access checks bound to your account. Transmission over the internet is never completely secure, so we cannot give an absolute guarantee.
legal.privacyCookiesBody: We set no advertising or analytics cookies on the public pages. Only technically necessary entries are stored: a session token for signing in plus your language and theme preference on this device. No consent banner is required for that; as soon as additional services such as external analytics or marketing tools are added, a consent solution becomes necessary.
legal.privacyChangesBody: We update this privacy policy when features, service providers or the legal situation change. The version published on this page is authoritative; the date above states its status.
legal.privacyContactBody: Please direct privacy questions to us through the contact form. The reply address and, where one exists, the contact details of a data protection officer will be added in the imprint before launch.
legal.termsSubtitle: Terms for using the Presence website monitoring service — working draft, to be reviewed legally before launch.
legal.termsIntro: These terms and conditions govern the use of Presence. They are a working draft: the text describes what the product technically does but has not been reviewed by a lawyer. Content in square brackets must be decided and completed before launch.
legal.termsScopeBody: These terms apply to the use of the Presence website monitoring service. The contracting party is the provider named in the imprint; those details must be completed before launch.
legal.termsServiceBody: Presence monitors publicly retrievable properties of the domains you register — reachability, SSL certificates, DNS records, e-mail security records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), HTTP security headers and response times — and displays the results in your account. Results are snapshots from the moment of the respective scan. They are not a security certificate, not a penetration test and not legal or tax advice; complete detection of all vulnerabilities or a specific availability is not owed.
legal.termsAccountBody: You must provide accurate information when registering and keep your credentials secret. Activity through your account is attributed to you unless you report possible misuse without delay. We may suspend or delete accounts that violate these terms.
legal.termsUseIntro: You may only monitor websites that you own or for whose monitoring you hold explicit permission. In particular it is prohibited:
termsUseItems: carrying out attacks or penetration tests against third-party systems
circumventing technical protection measures or access restrictions
using the service unlawfully or violating applicable law
impairing the service or its infrastructure, for example through excessive automated requests
legal.termsBillingBody: The scope of the free and paid plans follows from the price overview inside the application. Paid subscriptions are billed in advance monthly or annually. Payment and invoicing run through Paddle as merchant of record. Whether checkout is activated depends on the configuration: as long as it is not activated, no paid subscription can be concluded and no payments are collected. Prices, usage limits (such as the number of websites and scan frequency) and features must be reconciled with the actually configured values before launch. Whether prices have to be shown inclusive or exclusive of VAT is a tax question to settle.
legal.termsTermBody: A paid subscription runs for the chosen billing period and renews automatically unless cancelled beforehand. You can cancel at any time in your account settings; cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period. Afterwards the limits of the free plan apply. What this means in detail for stored websites and results must be defined before launch.
legal.termsWithdrawalBody: If the offer also addresses consumers, a statutory right of withdrawal may exist. Whether an early start of the service, an express consent or a statutory exception applies in that case must be reviewed before launch. The withdrawal page summarises the status and forms part of these terms.
legal.termsWithdrawalLink: Notes on the right of withdrawal
legal.termsAvailabilityBody: We aim for reliable operation but do not owe a specific availability or uninterrupted reachability. Maintenance work and disruptions are possible; where feasible we announce planned maintenance in advance.
legal.termsLiabilityBody: The information, ratings and alerts from Presence are the output of a monitoring tool. We accept no responsibility for decisions you take on that basis, nor for downtime, security incidents or other events around your website. For indirect damage, lost profit and data loss we are liable only for intent, gross negligence or breach of a material contractual duty; in those cases liability is limited in amount. A cap at the fees paid most recently and the exclusion of mandatory statutory claims — for instance for injury to life, body or health and under product liability law — must be reviewed legally before launch; mandatory rights must not be excluded.
legal.termsChangesTitle: Changes to the service and to these terms
legal.termsChangesBody: We may develop the service further and change individual features as long as the core of the booked scope remains. We inform you about significant changes to these terms by e-mail or in the application. Whether continued use counts as acceptance or an express consent is required must be settled before launch.
legal.termsLawTitle: Governing law and place of jurisdiction
legal.termsLawBody: Governing law and place of jurisdiction must be determined before launch. Mandatory consumer protection rules of a consumer's country of residence remain unaffected. We deliberately leave no invented statement in this place.
legal.termsContactBody: Please direct questions about these terms to us through the contact form. Whether an obligation to inform about consumer dispute resolution exists must be reviewed before launch.

dnsChecker.metaDescription: Check your domain DNS records for free. Verify A, MX, CNAME, TXT and NS records instantly.
dnsChecker.intro: Inspect your domain's DNS records instantly. Verify A records, MX records, CNAME, TXT and NS records — no technical knowledge required.
faqQuestions: What DNS records does the checker look up?
Why would my DNS records change unexpectedly?
What is an MX record?
How long does it take for DNS changes to propagate?
faqAnswers: The DNS checker retrieves A records (your website IP), MX records (email routing), CNAME records, TXT records (including SPF and DMARC), and NS records (name servers).

DNS changes can happen due to account compromises, accidental modifications at your domain registrar, hosting migrations, or technical errors. Unexpected DNS changes are a red flag worth investigating immediately.
An MX (mail exchanger) record tells the internet which server receives email for your domain. If your MX records are incorrect or missing, email sent to your domain may not arrive.
DNS changes can take up to 48 hours to propagate globally, though most changes are visible within a few hours.
howItWorks: We query public DNS servers for your records

emailSecurityChecker.metaTitle: Free Email Security Checker — SPF, DKIM & DMARC | Presence
emailSecurityChecker.metaDescription: Check your email security configuration for free. Verify SPF, DKIM and DMARC records to protect your business from email spoofing.
emailSecurityChecker.intro: Check your SPF, DKIM and DMARC email security configuration in seconds. Protect your business email from spoofing and impersonation — explained in plain language.
faqQuestions: What do SPF, DKIM and DMARC do?
My business is small. Do I really need DMARC?
What does 'DMARC policy: none' mean?
Can this checker fix my email security?
faqAnswers: SPF specifies which servers are allowed to send email from your domain. DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to verify emails are authentic. DMARC tells email providers what to do when an email fails SPF or DKIM checks — and allows you to receive reports about fraudulent use of your domain.

Yes. Email impersonation doesn't only target large companies. Criminals impersonate small business emails to scam suppliers, customers, and staff. DMARC is free to implement and significantly reduces this risk.

A DMARC policy of 'none' means you're monitoring but not enforcing. Emails that fail verification are still delivered. Upgrading to 'quarantine' or 'reject' provides actual protection against spoofed emails.

The checker identifies issues and recommends what to add or change. Implementing the changes requires adding DNS records at your domain registrar or hosting provider — or asking your web developer to do so.
howItWorks: We look up your email security DNS records
Results show what's configured and what's missing

emailSecurity.h1: Email Security Monitoring — SPF, DKIM & DMARC
emailSecurity.intro: Criminals impersonate business emails to scam your customers. Properly configuring SPF, DKIM and DMARC protects your business email and helps your legitimate emails reach inboxes. Presence checks your email security configuration and tells you exactly what needs attention.
emailSecurity.problem: Most small business owners have never heard of SPF, DKIM or DMARC — yet a missing or misconfigured email security record means anyone can send emails that appear to come from your domain.
emailSecurity.solution: Presence checks your SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration and explains the results in plain language. No technical knowledge required — we tell you exactly what's working and what needs improvement.
benefits: Check SPF, DKIM and DMARC configuration
Specific recommendations to improve email security
Protection against email spoofing and phishing
howItWorksDescriptions: Presence looks up your DNS records to find your email security configuration.
We verify your SPF, DKIM and DMARC records and check for common problems.
You receive a plain-language summary: what's working, what needs attention, and what to do next.
faqQuestions: What are SPF, DKIM and DMARC?
Do I need technical knowledge to fix email security issues?
Why is DMARC important?
Will fixing email security affect my existing email?
faqAnswers: SPF, DKIM and DMARC are email authentication standards. SPF specifies which servers can send email on your behalf. DKIM adds a digital signature to your emails. DMARC tells email providers what to do with emails that fail verification. Together they significantly reduce email impersonation.
Not with Presence. We explain what needs to be done in simple terms. You (or your hosting provider) will need to add or update a DNS record, but we guide you through it.
Without DMARC, scammers can send emails that appear to come from your domain to deceive your customers. DMARC tells email providers to reject or quarantine those fake emails.
Done correctly, adding SPF, DKIM and DMARC will not affect your legitimate email. Presence will notify you if your monitoring detects any issues.

uptimeMonitoring.title: Uptime Monitoring
uptimeMonitoring.metaTitle: Website Uptime Monitoring for Small Businesses | Presence
uptimeMonitoring.metaDescription: Track your website uptime over time. Monitor availability, detect outages instantly and measure your website reliability.
uptimeMonitoring.intro: Uptime is one of the most important metrics for your business website. Presence tracks your website availability over time and gives you clear uptime statistics, so you always know how reliable your website has been.
uptimeMonitoring.problem: Without uptime monitoring, you have no record of how often your website has been offline, how long outages lasted, or whether your hosting provider is delivering on their promises.
uptimeMonitoring.solution: Presence monitors your website continuously and records every outage. You can view your uptime history, identify patterns, and hold your hosting provider accountable with hard data.
howItWorksDescriptions: Presence begins monitoring your uptime immediately.
Every check result is recorded, building your uptime history.
Access clear charts and statistics showing your website availability over time.
faqQuestions: What does 99.9% uptime mean?
How is uptime calculated?
What counts as downtime?
Can I download uptime reports?
faqAnswers: 99.9% uptime means your website was offline for approximately 8.7 hours per year, or 43.8 minutes per month. Even small reductions in uptime add up quickly.
Presence checks your website regularly and records whether it was reachable. Uptime is calculated as the percentage of checks where your website responded successfully.
Downtime is recorded when Presence cannot reach your website or when your website returns an error response. Brief slow responses may not be counted as downtime.
Yes. Presence Pro and Business plans include downloadable PDF reports with your uptime statistics.

websitePerformance.title: Website Performance Monitoring
websitePerformance.metaDescription: Track your website response time and loading speed. Identify performance issues that affect your customers and search rankings.
websitePerformance.intro: A slow website frustrates visitors and hurts your search rankings. Presence tracks your website response time and loading speed, and alerts you when performance drops below acceptable levels.
websitePerformance.problem: Website performance degrades gradually. Without monitoring, you might not notice your website getting slower until visitors are already leaving in frustration or your search rankings have dropped.
websitePerformance.solution: Presence measures your website response time on every check and maintains a history of performance data. You can see exactly when performance changed and identify potential causes.
benefits: Response time tracking on every check
Alerts when response time exceeds thresholds
Performance as part of your Digital Health Score
howItWorksDescriptions: Presence immediately measures your website's response time.
Response time is measured on every check and recorded over time.
You're alerted if performance degrades, with clear recommendations to improve.
faqQuestions: What is website response time?
Does website speed affect SEO?
What causes slow website performance?
What is a good response time?
faqAnswers: Response time is how quickly your website server responds to a request. Fast response times (under 200ms) provide a good experience; slow response times (over 1000ms) can frustrate visitors.
Yes. Google considers page speed as a ranking factor. A slow website can rank lower in search results, reducing your organic traffic.
Common causes include unoptimized images, too many plugins, slow hosting, large JavaScript files, and database issues. Presence identifies the issue and recommends actions.
Under 200ms is excellent. Under 500ms is good. Over 1 second starts to affect user experience and should be investigated.

securityHeaders.title: Security Headers
securityHeaders.metaDescription: Check your website's HTTP security headers. Identify missing or misconfigured security headers that could put your visitors at risk.
securityHeaders.intro: Security headers are simple configuration settings that protect your visitors from common web attacks. Many small business websites are missing these basic protections. Presence checks your security headers and tells you exactly what to improve — in plain language.
securityHeaders.problem: Security headers are invisible to most website owners. Missing headers can expose your visitors to clickjacking, cross-site scripting (XSS), and other common web attacks.
securityHeaders.solution: Presence checks your website's security headers and explains each finding in plain language. We don't just report the technical details — we tell you what the risk is and what to do about it.
benefits: Security headers as part of your Digital Health Score
howItWorksDescriptions: Presence reads your website's HTTP response headers.
We check for the presence and correct configuration of important security headers.
You receive a clear summary of what's configured, what's missing, and what to add.
faqQuestions: What are security headers?
Which security headers does Presence check?
Do I need to be technical to fix security header issues?
Will adding security headers break my website?
faqAnswers: Security headers are HTTP response headers that your server sends to browsers. They instruct browsers how to behave to protect your visitors — for example, preventing your website from being embedded in an iframe on another site.
Presence checks for Content-Security-Policy (CSP), Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.
Not with Presence. We explain what needs to be done in plain language. Your hosting provider or website developer can implement the changes with our recommendations.
Some headers (like CSP) need careful configuration to avoid breaking functionality. Presence always recommends a safe starting configuration and explains any trade-offs.

reviewMonitoring.title: Review Monitoring
reviewMonitoring.metaTitle: Online Review Monitoring for Small Businesses | Presence
reviewMonitoring.metaDescription: Monitor your online reviews and customer ratings. Stay on top of new reviews and respond quickly to negative feedback.
reviewMonitoring.h1: Online Review Monitoring for Small Businesses
reviewMonitoring.intro: Online reviews are one of the first things potential customers check before visiting your business. Presence monitors your customer ratings across platforms and alerts you when new reviews arrive — so you can respond quickly.
reviewMonitoring.problem: A single unanswered negative review can deter dozens of potential customers. Most business owners only check their reviews occasionally — by which time the damage to their reputation may already be done.
reviewMonitoring.solution: Presence monitors your online reviews and notifies you when new reviews arrive. For negative reviews, Presence can suggest a response using AI — which you review and approve before it's ever sent.
benefits: Alerts when negative reviews need attention
howItWorksDescriptions: Tell Presence where your business appears online.
Presence tracks new reviews as they arrive.
You're notified immediately and can draft a response with AI assistance.
faqQuestions: Which review platforms does Presence monitor?
Does Presence post responses automatically?
How quickly am I notified about new reviews?
Does responding to reviews help my business?
faqAnswers: Presence monitors Google Reviews and Yelp. Additional platforms are on the roadmap.
Never. Presence can suggest AI-generated responses, but you always review, edit, and approve any response before it is published. We believe in human oversight.
Presence checks for new reviews regularly and notifies you promptly when a new review is detected.
Yes. Responding to reviews — especially negative ones — shows potential customers that you care about feedback. Businesses that respond to reviews consistently score higher in trust ratings.
